item.title: Higher Ed Startup Uses AI to Help Colleges Prevent Dropouts
item.description: Straia, a higher-education startup focused on data analytics, has raised $3.1 million from investors to help schools tackle issues like student retention.

item.title: French Riots Seen as Insurance Test Before New Regime Kicks In
item.description: The damage wrought cross France by the recent street riots will demonstrate the extent of current insurance coverage, just months before a new state-backed system kicks in, according to DBRS Morningstar analysts.

item.title: Iran Strikes More Ship Engine Rooms in Ramp-Up of Hormuz Attacks
item.description: Iranian attacks in the Persian Gulf are striking more ships and causing more severe damage than earlier in the conflict, bringing fresh risks to energy flows from the region.

item.title: GM Narrows 2026 Profit Forecast, Boosts Share Buyback
item.description: General Motors narrowed its full-year profit forecast amid softening sales, while also announcing it will buy back another $20 billion in stock. Paul Jacobson, CFO and executive vice president at GM, discusses the results on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia Ships the Least Oil in a Month as Major Baltic Port Halts
item.description: Shipments from key port of Primorsk tumbled last week, likely on maintenance work

item.title: New York Arrests 16 in Crackdown on Staged Insurance Crashes
item.description: New York state investigators arrested 16 people accused of staging car crashes and faking injuries to collect nearly $500,000 from insurers, one of the first major enforcement actions since Governor Kathy Hochul made auto insurance fraud a focus of her effort to lower costs for drivers.

item.title: Airport Near Coachella, Palm Springs Eyes $174 Million Muni Sale
item.description: The Ontario International Airport, a gateway to the popular desert destinations of Southern California’s Inland Empire, is tapping the municipal bond market for roughly $174 million to fund various improvements.

item.title: Stocks Slip as AI Infrastructure IPO Flops, SpaceX Results Loom
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index opened lower on Tuesday, as South Korean neocloud company Elice Inc.’s debut tanked, spurring concern about the sustainability of the global AI boom. Investors are also on edge ahead of a spate of tech earnings this week, including SpaceX and Netflix Inc. after the bell.

item.title: AI Fears Return With Data Center IPO Flop; SpaceX, Netflix Earnings
item.description: US equity futures slip, pausing an AI recovery in stocks, after South Korean data center company Elice plunged in its trading debut. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy heads to Norway for fresh peace talks as tensions with the US deepens. SpaceX, Netflix, General Motors, RTX, and Northrop are set to report earnings. Jeanne Sun of Citigroup Global Markets joins "Bloomberg Brief" to discuss her outlook for this earnings season. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Heading for a Slowdown, Not a Recession, Says Crossmark’s Fernandez
item.description: Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments, explains the factors she sees pointing to a slowdown in the US economy and markets. She speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Storm Austen to Boost Wind Power in Europe as Gas Prices Surge
item.description: The first named storm of this autumn is set to lash the UK and northwest Europe with heavy rain and wind in the coming days, potentially bringing some relief to elevated power prices.

item.title: Halliburton Sees Lasting Growth as Mideast Rebuilds From War
item.description: Halliburton Co. is predicting years of growth for oil field service work as nations replenish crude reserves and the Middle East rebuilds infrastructure damaged in the Iran war.

item.title: European Gas Prices Rise Above €90 for First Time Since 2022
item.description: European natural gas climbed above €90 for the first time in almost four years, raising the threat of a renewed energy crunch as Europe heads into the peak winter heating season.

item.title: Partners Group Cuts Management Fees Before Fund Overhaul
item.description: Partners Group Holding AG is reducing management fees at a key evergreen fund as it seeks investor approval to revamp the private equity vehicle.

item.title: Netflix Needs Blockbusters to Reverse Its $135 Billion Wipeout
item.description: Netflix Inc. needs to prove that it can produce hit movies and TV series again to stop a slide that has erased more than $135 billion in market value this year.

item.title: French Bond Risk Climbs Again With Investors Wary on Outlook
item.description: A measure of French bond risk breached a key level on Tuesday, underscoring the challenges facing the government as it struggles to tame the budget deficit and grapples with cost-of-living protests.

item.title: Maersk, Hateco Plan $3.5 Billion Vietnam Freight Network
item.description: A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S, the world’s No. 2 container carrier, signed an agreement with Vietnamese conglomerate Hateco to develop a railway freight terminal network in Vietnam during President To Lam’s official visit to Denmark.

item.title: Corn Rises From Two-Month Low After Recent Drop Seen Overdone
item.description: Corn futures edged higher in Chicago amid technical signals that its five-day losing streak was overdone.

item.title: Stocks Fall as AI Worries Trigger Treasury Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Renewed selling in chipmakers dragged down stocks as the dismal debut of a South Korean data center firm revived concerns about the artificial-intelligence trade.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 20
item.description: Brent oil climbed to a five-month high as traders weighed the threat of Iranian strikes hampering energy flows, with fuel prices around the world already elevated.
